questions.question: Who was appointed as Chairperson of the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister (EAC‑PM) in June 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**S Mahendra Dev**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **S Mahendra Dev** was appointed as the **Chairperson** of the **Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister (EAC-PM)** in **June 2025**.
 
• He is a distinguished **economist** who previously served as the **Director and Vice-Chancellor** of the **Indira Gandhi Institute of Development Research (IGIDR)** in **Mumbai**.
 
• The **EAC-PM** is an **independent body** constituted to provide economic advice specifically to the **Prime Minister of India** on both macro and microeconomic matters.
 
• **S Mahendra Dev** has a notable career in policy-making, having served as the **Chairman** of the **Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP)** under the **Ministry of Agriculture**.
 
• His appointment follows the tenure of **Bibek Debroy**, who was a long-standing head of the council since its reconstitution in **2017**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister (EAC-PM):**
 
 
• The council is tasked with **analyzing any issue**, economic or otherwise, referred to it by the **Prime Minister**.
 
• It addresses **macroeconomic importance** and presents views to the Prime Minister; this could be either **suo-motu** or on reference.
 
• The **administrative, logistic, and financial** requirements of the **EAC-PM** are met by the **NITI Aayog**, which serves as the **Nodal Agency**.
 
 
 
• **Structure of the Council:**
 
 
• The council typically includes a **Chairperson**, **Full-time Members**, and several **Part-time Members** who are usually eminent experts from academia or research institutions.
 
• The **terms of reference** include analyzing **economic trends** and advising on **policy interventions**.
 
 
 
• **Other Options Explained:**
 
 
• **Suman Bery**: He is a veteran economist who took over as the **Vice Chairperson** of **NITI Aayog** in **May 2022**, succeeding Rajiv Kumar.
 
• **Bibek Debroy**: A prominent Indian economist and Indologist who served as the **Chairman** of the **EAC-PM** from its revival in **September 2017**.
 
• **Arun Kumar**: Often refers to the noted **Professor** and expert on the **Black Economy** in India, known for his critical analysis of **demonetization** and **GST**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **EAC-PM** was reconstituted in **2017** after a gap; it replaced the previous council that existed during the **UPA** era under **C. Rangarajan**.
 
• Unlike **NITI Aayog**, which is a statutory-like policy think tank with a broad developmental mandate, the **EAC-PM** focuses specifically on **immediate economic advice** for the head of the government.
 
• **S Mahendra Dev** holds a **Ph.D.** from the **Delhi School of Economics** and completed his **Post-doctoral research** at **Yale University**.
 
• The **appointment** of such experts is crucial for navigating **inflationary pressures**, **GDP growth targets**, and **fiscal deficit** management in the **Indian Economy**.
</ul

questions.question: According to Reporters Without Borders (RSF) World Press Freedom Index 2025, which country topped the index released in May 2025?
questions.solution:
p data-end="57" data-start="0">The correct answer is __**Norway**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **World Press Freedom Index 2025** was released by the international non-governmental organization **Reporters Without Borders (RSF)** in **May 2025**.
 
• **Norway** secured the **first rank** in the index, continuing its long-standing streak as the world's most free country for journalists and media organizations.
 
• The index is typically unveiled on **May 3rd**, which is observed globally as **World Press Freedom Day** to highlight the importance of independent media.
 
• **Norway**'s top position is attributed to its strong **constitutional protections** for freedom of speech and a diverse media landscape that operates without political or economic interference.
 
• Following **Norway**, other **Nordic** and **European** nations such as **Denmark**, **Sweden**, and **Estonia** frequently occupy the top five positions in the global rankings.
 
• The **2025** edition of the index evaluates the state of journalism in **180 countries** and territories, focusing on the ability of journalists to report news without fear of reprisal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Reporters Without Borders (RSF):**
 
 
• It is a **Paris-based** non-profit organization founded in **1985** by **Robert Ménard**, **Rémy Loury**, **Jacques Molénat**, and **Émilien Jubineau**.
 
• **RSF** holds consultative status with the **United Nations**, **UNESCO**, and the **Council of Europe**.
 
• The organization acts as a watchdog to defend **freedom of information** and provides assistance to journalists working in war zones.
 
 
 
• **Methodology of the Index:**
 
 
• The ranking is determined based on **five contextual indicators**: **Political context**, **Legal framework**, **Economic context**, **Sociocultural context**, and **Safety**.
 
• A quantitative tally of abuses against journalists and a qualitative analysis based on a survey of hundreds of **press freedom experts** are used to calculate the final score.
 
• The scores range from **0 to 100**, with **100** representing the highest possible level of press freedom.
 
 
 
• **Global Trends in 2025:**
 
 
• The **2025** report expressed concerns regarding the rise of **Generative AI** and its role in spreading **disinformation** and "deepfakes."
 
• It also noted a decline in press freedom in regions facing active conflicts, where **censorship** and physical violence against reporters have increased.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **India's Performance:**
 
 
• In recent years, **India** has seen a decline in its ranking, often placing in the **"Difficult"** category. In the **2024** index, **India** was ranked **159th** out of **180 countries**.
 
• Common challenges cited for **India** include **restrictive laws**, physical attacks on journalists, and the concentration of media ownership.
 
 
 
• **Bottom of the Index:**
 
 
• Countries that consistently rank at the bottom (around **178th to 180th**) include **Eritrea**, **North Korea**, and **Afghanistan**, where independent journalism is virtually non-existent.
 
• These nations are often categorized as having a **"Very Serious"** situation regarding press freedom.
 
 
 
• **Regional Insights:**
 
 
• The **Maghreb** and **Middle East** regions remain among the most dangerous places for journalists globally due to ongoing instability and **authoritarian regimes**.
 
• The **European Union** remains the region where press freedom is best protected, although it faces internal challenges from **populist movements** in certain member states.
 
 

2f

questions.question: As per the India Justice Report, 2025, which is the only state in India to meet all three (SC, ST and OBC) quotas in both the police and judiciary?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Karnataka**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **India Justice Report (IJR) 2025** identifies **Karnataka** as the standout performer in maintaining social diversity within its justice delivery system.
 
• It is currently the **only state in India** to have successfully met the prescribed reservation quotas for **Scheduled Castes (SC)**, **Scheduled Tribes (ST)**, and **Other Backward Classes (OBC)** in both its **Police** department and the **Judiciary**.
 
• In the **Police** pillar, **Karnataka** has demonstrated a consistent ability to fill **reserved vacancies**, ensuring that the law enforcement agency reflects the demographic composition of the state.
 
• In the **Judiciary** pillar, particularly at the **subordinate court level**, the state has adhered to the **Constitutional mandates** of representation for marginalized communities, which is a rare feat across Indian states.
 
• Overall, **Karnataka** ranked **first** among the 18 large and mid-sized states in the **India Justice Report**, maintaining its leadership position in the overall capacity to deliver justice. ***Hence, the correct answer is Karnataka.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About India Justice Report (IJR):**
 
 
• The **IJR** is a first-of-its-kind initiative launched in **2019** by **Tata Trusts** in collaboration with partners such as **Centre for Social Justice**, **Common Cause**, **Commonwealth Human Rights Initiative**, **DAKSH**, **TISS-Prayas**, and **Vidhi Centre for Legal Policy**.
 
• It tracks the **capacity** of states to deliver justice based on **four pillars**: **Police**, **Prisons**, **Judiciary**, and **Legal Aid**.
 
• The report uses **government data** to assess states on various parameters including **budgets**, **human resources**, **workload**, **diversity**, **infrastructure**, and **trends** over the last five years.
 
 
 
• **Diversity and Representation:**
 
 
• The report highlights that **diversity** is a crucial indicator of a fair justice system. Nationally, most states struggle to meet **SC, ST, and OBC** quotas, leading to significant **vacancies**.
 
• While **Karnataka** leads in caste-based quotas, the report also examines **Women in Justice**. It notes that while the share of women is increasing, they still represent a small fraction of the **Police** and **Judiciary** at higher levels across **India**.
 
 
 
• **Performance of Other States:**
 
 
• In the **2025** ranking, states like **Tamil Nadu**, **Telangana**, and **Gujarat** followed **Karnataka** in the top tier of large states.
 
• Smaller states like **Sikkim** and **Arunachal Pradesh** are ranked separately, with **Sikkim** often performing well in the small states category.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Constitutional Provisions:**
 
 
• The reservation for **SC, ST, and OBC** in public employment and services is backed by **Articles 15(4)** and **16(4)** of the **Constitution of India**.
 
• Ensuring representation in the **Judiciary** and **Police** is vital for maintaining the **Rule of Law** and building **public trust** in the state's institutions.
 
 
 
• **Key National Findings:**
 
 
• Despite the progress in **Karnataka**, the **IJR 2025** points out a **national trend** of rising **pendency** of cases and chronic **under-staffing** in prisons and courts.
 
• The average vacancy in **High Courts** remains high at nearly **30%**, and the **Police-to-Population ratio** remains below international standards in many states.
 
• The report serves as a **policy tool** for **State Governments** and the **Union Government** to address systemic gaps in the **Indian justice system**.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Which global cybersecurity company collaborated with the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) to launch the Digital Threat Report 2024 for the Banking, Financial Services, and Insurance (BFSI) sector in April 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**SISA**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The global cybersecurity company **SISA**, known for its forensic-driven approach, collaborated with the **Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In)** to launch the **Digital Threat Report 2024** for the **Banking, Financial Services, and Insurance (BFSI)** sector in **April 2025**.
 
• The report serves as a comprehensive guide for financial institutions to understand the evolving landscape of **cyber threats**, providing actionable insights to strengthen their **cybersecurity posture**.
 
• The collaboration highlights the importance of **Public-Private Partnerships (PPP)** in safeguarding the national **critical information infrastructure**, particularly the financial backbone of the country.
 
• Key findings in the report emphasize the rise of **sophisticated cyber-attacks** targeting digital payment gateways, mobile banking applications, and insurance databases within the **BFSI sector**.
 
• The report outlines specific **mitigation strategies** and **security frameworks** that organizations should adopt to counter threats like **ransomware**, **advanced persistent threats (APTs)**, and **AI-driven fraud**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **SISA:**
 
 
• **SISA** is a global **forensics-driven cybersecurity** company headquartered in **Bengaluru**, **India**, with a strong presence in regions like the **Middle East**, **USA**, and **South East Asia**.
 
• It is a **PCI Qualified Security Assessor (QSA)** and an authorized **Forensic Investigator (PFI)**, helping organizations comply with global standards like **PCI DSS**.
 
• The company focuses on **security compliance**, **technical audits**, and **managed detection and response (MDR)** services.
 
 
 
• **CERT-In (Indian Computer Emergency Response Team):**
 
 
• It is the national nodal agency for responding to **computer security incidents** as and when they occur, operating under the **Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)**.
 
• **CERT-In** was established in **2004** under the **Information Technology Act, 2000**.
 
• Its primary functions include **incident reporting**, issuing **advisories**, **vulnerability notes**, and conducting **cybersecurity training** for various sectors.
 
 
 
• **BFSI Sector Vulnerabilities:**
 
 
• The **BFSI sector** is a prime target for **cybercriminals** due to the high volume of **financial transactions** and sensitive **personal data** involved.
 
• Common threats include **Phishing**, **Vishing**, **Credential Stuffing**, and the use of **Deepfakes** for identity theft in the **Know Your Customer (KYC)** process.
 
• Regulations from the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** and **SEBI** mandate strict **cyber-resilience** norms for banks and intermediaries.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Emerging Threats in 2024-2025:** The report specifically identifies **Generative AI** as a double-edged sword, used by attackers to create more convincing **malware** and by defenders for **threat hunting**.
 
• **Regulatory Compliance:** Financial institutions are encouraged to align with the **Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act, 2023**, to ensure the privacy of customer information during **data breaches**.
 
• **Global Context:** Similar reports are published globally by entities like **INTERPOL** and **FS-ISAC** to track **transnational cybercrime** trends affecting the **global financial system**.
 
• **Digital Payment Security:** With the massive adoption of **UPI (Unified Payments Interface)** in **India**, the report provides a dedicated section on securing **real-time payment ecosystems**.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following countries is the venue for the 2025 Esports World Cup?

__
 
• **Riyadh**, the capital of **Saudi Arabia**, has been designated as the permanent host city for the **Esports World Cup (EWC)**, including the upcoming **2025** edition.
 
• The tournament is an annual international esports competition that replaced the previous **Gamers8** festival, which was also held in **Saudi Arabia**.
 
• The announcement of the **Esports World Cup** was made by **Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman** in **October 2023**, aiming to establish the kingdom as a premier global hub for gaming and esports.
 
• The **Esports World Cup Foundation**, a non-profit organization, is responsible for organizing the event and managing the massive scale of the competition.
 
• The event features a unique **cross-game competition** format where professional esports clubs from across the globe compete in various titles to earn points for a collective club championship. ***Hence, the correct answer is Riyadh.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• It aims to increase the sector's contribution to the **GDP** by more than **SAR 50 billion** (approximately **$13.3 billion**) by **2030**.
 
• The strategy intends to create **39,000 new job opportunities** within the gaming industry by the end of the decade.
 
 
 
• **Vision 2030 and Economic Diversification:**
 
 
• **Saudi Arabia** is investing heavily in the **entertainment and sports** sectors to reduce its economic reliance on oil.
 
• The **Public Investment Fund (PIF)** has established **Savvy Games Group**, which has spent billions of dollars acquiring major gaming entities like **ESL FaceIt Group** and **Scopely**.

• The event attracts millions of viewers globally and brings together elite athletes from games such as **League of Legends**, **Dota 2**, **Counter-Strike 2**, **StarCraft II**, and **Mobile Legends: Bang Bang**.

• **Tournament Structure:**
 
 
• Unlike traditional single-title tournaments, the **Esports World Cup** focuses on **Club Excellence**. This means organizations like **Team Liquid**, **FaZe Clan**, or **G2 Esports** compete across multiple games to be crowned the ultimate champion club.
 
• The **2025** edition is expected to expand even further with more game titles and a larger qualifying structure involving regional qualifiers in **Europe**, **Asia**, and the **Americas**.
 
 
 
• **Infrastructure:**
 
 
• The venue in **Riyadh** features state-of-the-art facilities at **Boulevard City**, including specialized arenas for different game genres (FPS, MOBA, Battle Royale).
 
• This infrastructure is designed to accommodate the **summer season** peak, making **Riyadh** a major tourist destination during the tournament months.

questions.question: Which of the following is India's rank among the most polluted countries of the world as of IQ Air Report 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• According to the **IQAir World Air Quality Report 2023**, which was released in **March 2024**, **India** has been ranked as the **3rd** most polluted country in the world. 
• The report analyzed data from **134** countries, regions, and territories, focusing on **PM2.5** concentrations, which are fine particulate matter particles that pose the greatest risk to human health. 
• **India's** average annual **PM2.5** concentration was recorded at **54.4 micrograms per cubic meter (µg/m³)**, which is more than **10 times** higher than the **WHO** (World Health Organization) annual air quality guideline. 
• In the previous year's report (data for **2022**), **India** was ranked **8th**, indicating a significant deterioration in air quality as it jumped to the **3rd** position in the **2024** report. 
• The top two most polluted countries ahead of **India** are **Bangladesh** (ranked **1st** with **79.9 µg/m³**) and **Pakistan** (ranked **2nd** with **73.7 µg/m³**). 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **IQAir** is a **Swiss** air quality technology company that prepares this annual report by aggregating data from over **30,000** air quality monitoring stations globally. 
• **Begusarai**, a city in Bihar, **India**, emerged as the world's most polluted metropolitan area in the **2024** report, with an average annual **PM2.5** concentration of **118.9 µg/m³**. 
• **Delhi** has once again been identified as the most polluted **capital city** in the world. It has held this undesirable title **four** times since **2018**. 
• The **WHO** air quality guidelines recommend that annual average levels of **PM2.5** should not exceed **5 µg/m³**. Approximately **92.5%** of the countries and regions reporting data exceeded this value. 
• Air pollution remains a critical health crisis in **South Asia**, with **9** out of the **10** most polluted cities in the world being located in this region, primarily across **India** and **Pakistan**. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• The **PM2.5** particles are so small (less than **2.5 micrometers** in diameter) that they can enter the bloodstream and cause various respiratory and cardiovascular diseases. 
• In **India**, about **1.3 billion** people, or **96%** of the population, live with air quality that is **seven times** higher than the **WHO** guideline. 
• Factors contributing to high pollution in **India** include **vehicle emissions**, **coal burning** for power generation, **industrial waste**, **biomass burning** for cooking, and **construction dust**.

questions.question: The Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025 mandates the representation of how many Muslim women on Waqf boards?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Two**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Waqf (Amendment) Bill**, introduced in **August 2024** (often discussed in context of its upcoming implementation in **2025**), proposes a mandatory representation of **two Muslim women** on both the **Central Waqf Council** and the **State Waqf Boards**.
 
• This provision is aimed at ensuring **gender diversity** and empowering women in the administrative decision-making processes of **Waqf properties**, which was previously dominated by male representation.
 
• Under the proposed amendments to the **Waqf Act, 1995**, the composition of the **State Waqf Boards** will be expanded to include not only Muslim women but also **two non-Muslim members**, ensuring a more inclusive governance structure.
 
• The **Union Minister of Minority Affairs**, **Shri Kiren Rijiju**, introduced the bill to bring transparency and efficiency, noting that the inclusion of **two Muslim women** is a historic step toward reform within the community's socio-religious institutions.
 
• The bill also mandates that the **Central Waqf Council** must include **two Muslim women** among its members, who are appointed by the **Central Government**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Waqf Act, 1995:**
 
 
• This is the primary legislation governing **Waqf institutions** in India. A **Waqf** is a permanent dedication of property for **religious, pious, or charitable** purposes under **Muslim Law**.
 
• The **1995 Act** replaced the earlier **Waqf Act of 1954** and was significantly amended in **2013** to provide more powers to the **Waqf Boards**.
 
 
 
• **Proposed Changes in the 2024/2025 Amendment:**
 
 
• The new bill seeks to rename the **Waqf Act, 1995** as the **Unified Waqf Management, Empowerment, Efficiency and Development Act**.
 
• It proposes that any property identified as **Waqf property** must undergo a mandatory **verification process** through the **District Collector** to prevent disputes.
 
• The amendment also states that only a person who has been practicing **Islam for at least five years** can donate property as **Waqf** (Waqif).
 
 
 
• **Central Waqf Council:**
 
 
• Established in **1964**, it is an **Indian statutory body** that advises the **Central Government** on matters concerning the working of **State Waqf Boards**.
 
• The Council is headed by the **Union Minister** in charge of **Minority Affairs**, who acts as the **Ex-officio Chairperson**.
 
 
 
• **Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC):**
 
 
• Following its introduction in the **Lok Sabha** in **2024**, the **Waqf (Amendment) Bill** was referred to a **Joint Parliamentary Committee** for detailed scrutiny due to its complex socio-legal implications.
 
• The committee consists of members from both the **Lok Sabha** and the **Rajya Sabha** to review the clauses concerning **women's representation** and the **Collector's powers**.

questions.question: Which religious communities are covered under Karnataka’s ₹50,000 incentive scheme for mass marriages in July 2025?

options.text: Muslim, Christian, Jain, Buddhist, Parsi and Sikh

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Muslim, Christian, Jain, Buddhist, Parsi and Sikh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Karnataka Government**, through its **Minority Welfare Department**, provides financial incentives to encourage mass marriages among minority communities to reduce the financial burden on poor families.
 
• As per the latest directives and scheme updates for **July 2025**, the incentive amount for couples participating in these mass marriages has been set at **₹50,000**.
 
• The scheme specifically covers the six notified minority communities in the state: **Muslim, Christian, Jain, Buddhist, Parsi, and Sikh**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Muslim, Christian, Jain, Buddhist, Parsi and Sikh.***
 
• The primary objective of this initiative is to prevent **Below Poverty Line (BPL)** families from falling into debt traps due to high wedding expenses and to promote the concept of simple, community-led weddings.
 
• To avail of this benefit, the **combined annual income** of the couple’s parents or the couple themselves must typically fall below a specified threshold, often **₹2 lakh** or less, depending on the latest department guidelines.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Eligibility Criteria:**
 
 
• Applicants must be **permanent residents** of **Karnataka**.
 
• The bride must have attained the age of **18 years** and the groom must be at least **21 years** old, adhering to the **Prohibition of Child Marriage Act**.
 
• The beneficiaries must belong to the **Minority Community** as defined by the **National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992**.
 
 
 
• **Required Documentation:**
 
 
• Valid **Aadhar Card** of both the bride and the groom for identity verification.
 
• **BPL (Below Poverty Line) Card** or an **Income Certificate** issued by the **Tahsildar**.
 
• **Caste/Minority Certificate** to prove eligibility under the specific religious categories.
 
• **Bank Account** details linked with Aadhar (Direct Benefit Transfer - **DBT**) for the disbursement of the **₹50,000** incentive.
 
 
 
• **Scheme Administration:**
 
 
• The scheme is implemented by the **Directorate of Minorities** in **Karnataka**.
 
• Applications are usually processed through the **Seva Sindhu** portal or directly through the **District Minority Welfare Offices**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Evolution of Welfare Schemes:** This incentive is often compared to the **"Shadi Bhagya"** (also known as the **Bidai Scheme**) launched in **2013**, which initially provided **₹50,000** for the marriage of poor minority women.
 
• **Mass Marriage Focus:** Unlike individual grants, the **mass marriage incentive** specifically rewards participation in organized group ceremonies to foster social harmony and communal cooperation.
 
• **Saptapadi Scheme:** For the **Hindu** community, the **Karnataka Government** runs a parallel program called the **Saptapadi** scheme under the **Muzrai Department**, which provides **gold mangalsutras** and cash incentives for mass marriages held in selected temples.
 
• **Social Impact:** By providing **₹50,000**, the state aims to empower **marginalized religious groups** and ensure that social ceremonies do not lead to **economic distress** or **bonded labor** due to private loans.

questions.question: According to Envstats India 2025, what was the inland fish production in 2023-24?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**139.07 lakh tonnes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **Envstats India 2025** report (and recent data from the **Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying**), India's total fish production has shown a consistent upward trajectory, with the **inland fish production** specifically reaching **139.07 lakh tonnes** during the **2023-24** financial year.
 
• Inland fisheries have become the primary driver of the sector's growth, contributing significantly more than the marine sector. The production has increased from **131.13 lakh tonnes** in **2022-23** to the current figure, reflecting a steady growth rate. ***Hence, the correct answer is 139.07 lakh tonnes.***
 
• The **inland sector** now accounts for approximately **79%** of the total fish production in the country, showcasing a shift from traditional marine fishing to **aquaculture** and fresh-water resources.
 
• The **Department of Fisheries** has highlighted that the consistent rise is due to improved infrastructure, better seeds, and the adoption of modern technology like **Recirculatory Aquaculture Systems (RAS)** and **Biofloc**.
 
• This growth is pivotal for **food security** and providing **livelihood** to over **30 million** people, particularly those in the marginalized and **unorganized sectors**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY):**
 
 
• Launched in **May 2020**, this flagship scheme aims to bring about the **Blue Revolution** through sustainable and responsible development of the fisheries sector.
 
• It has an estimated investment of **Rs. 20,050 crores** for a period of **5 years** (FY 2020-21 to FY 2024-25).
 
• The scheme focuses on enhancing fish production to **22 million metric tonnes** by **2024-25** and doubling the incomes of **fishers** and **fish farmers**.
 
 
 
• **India's Global Standing:**
 
 
• India is currently the **third-largest** fish-producing country in the world.
 
• It occupies the **second** position in **aquaculture** production globally.
 
• The fisheries sector contributes about **1.09%** to the total **National GVA** and over **6.72%** to the **Agricultural GVA**.
 
 
 
• **Marine Fish Production:**
 
 
• While inland fish production reached **139.07 lakh tonnes**, marine fish production for **2023-24** stood at approximately **36.38 lakh tonnes**.
 
• The total fish production (Inland + Marine) for the year **2023-24** is estimated at **175.45 lakh tonnes**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF):**
 
 
• Created in **2018-19** with a corpus of **Rs. 7,522.48 crore** to provide concessional finance to State Governments and private entities for fisheries infrastructure.
 
• It supports the creation of **fishing harbours**, **fish landing centres**, and **cold storage** facilities.
 
 
 
• **Blue Economy 2.0:**
 
 
• The **Interim Budget 2024-25** emphasized the **Blue Economy 2.0** to promote climate-resilient activities and restoration/adaptation measures along the coastline.
 
• Five **integrated aqua parks** are being set up to bolster value chain efficiencies and exports.
 
 
 
• **State-wise Production:**
 
 
• **Andhra Pradesh** continues to be the leading producer of inland fish in India, followed by states like **West Bengal** and **Uttar Pradesh**.
 
 
</ul
